claims.claim: Making a small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: Timing matters. A payment by the party to be charged toward principal or interest due on a promissory note starts a new period before the claim is barred. Once barred, such a payment alone does not revive the claim.

claims.claim: Signing something on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The contents of the writing matter. The statute does not rule out a new or continuing contract evidenced by an acknowledgment or promise signed by the party to be charged.

claims.claim: The applicable limit is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Section 337 specifies the actions it covers. The stated scope identifies debts by proximity to a deadline, not by whether section 337 applies.

claims.claim: The four-year limit keeps running no matter what the person pays or signs.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: Section 337 expressly allows extension under section 360.

claims.claim: You can safely make a payment.
claims.quote: the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: The assurance conflicts with the consequence of a qualifying promissory-note payment before the claim is barred.

claims.claim: You can safely sign a payment plan.
claims.quote: unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: A plan may contain a signed acknowledgment or promise. The source gives no blanket assurance about signing one.

flags.text: The claim that the period always keeps running conflicts with section 360's new-period rule.
The draft does not distinguish a near-barred claim from an already barred one, a qualifying note payment from other payments, or a signed acknowledgment or promise from other signed documents.
The scope does not identify debts covered by section 337, and the answer treats every payment and signed writing alike.
“You can safely” directs the reader to act without checking the debt, timing, or terms of the writing.
Relying on the assurance could lead someone to start a new period by paying on a note near the limit or to weaken a limitations defense by signing an acknowledgment or promise.

result.summary: Section 360 distinguishes starting a new period before a claim is barred from reviving an already barred claim by payment alone. It also makes the content of a signed writing relevant. Neither assurance of safety is supported.
